mainTopic: מעילה on a consecrated בור and שובך: the empty case (דבר שלא בא לעולם) and the full case (learning הקדש from an ordinary sale)
overview: The גמרא shows that רבה's first version can't be right, so it rewords it. The מחלוקת between the תנא קמא and רבי אלעזר בר' שמעון is only about a בור (cistern) and a שובך (dovecote). For a field and a tree, everyone agrees there is מעילה on the item and on what is in it. When the בור or שובך is empty, the argument is the famous one between רבי מאיר and the רבנן about transferring a דבר שלא בא לעולם. רבא answers a challenge to this by showing cases where the water or doves really are expected to come. When the בור is full and was consecrated סתם, the question is whether we learn הקדש from an ordinary sale (דנין דין גבוה מדין הדיוט). If we do, then just as a seller can keep the water, the water is not consecrated. The גמרא then challenges this from our משנה, which says selling a cistern includes its water. רבא answers that the משנה follows the lone view of רבי נתן.

steps.title: Why would he reverse the ruling for a field and a tree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that the מחלוקת is about a field and a tree: why would רבי אלעזר בר' שמעון reverse the ruling there?
steps.simpleTranslation: If the argument is about a field and a tree, why does he reverse the ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier claim that the argument is about a field and a tree. It asks why רבי אלעזר בר' שמעון would reverse the ruling in those cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בר' שמעון's view is described as reversing (מחליף) the ruling of the תנא קמא. The גמרא finds that hard to accept if the case is a field or a tree. This pressure forces רבה's statement to be reworded in the next step.

phrases.english: And if it is about a field and a tree,
why does he reverse?
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי אלעזר בר' שמעון, the one who argues with the תנא קמא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's earlier version, which put the מחלוקת in a field and a tree.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the מחלוקת is about a field and a tree
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is hard to explain why רבי אלעזר בר' שמעון would reverse the ruling in the case of a field and a tree.

steps.title: רבה reworded: the dispute is only about a cistern and a dovecote
steps.stepSummary: רבה's statement is reworded. The מחלוקת is about a בור and a שובך, and for a field and a tree everyone agrees there is מעילה on them and on what is in them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said: the argument is about a cistern and a dovecote. But for a field and a tree, everyone agrees there is מעילה on them and on what is inside them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רבה's statement by moving the argument to the cistern and dovecote. For a field and a tree, both sides agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The field and tree cases now become cases everyone agrees on: the consecrated item and its contents are both covered by מעילה. The cistern and dovecote are now the only cases still in dispute. That is why the next steps look closely at them.

keyTerms.meaning: One is liable for מעילה (misusing הקדש)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion from a different אמורא. It is the same רבה, with his statement reworded so it doesn't run into the problem from step 1.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba said:
The dispute is about a cistern and a dovecote,
but about a field and a tree,
everyone agrees one is liable for misuse of them
and of what is in them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by rewording רבה's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording the earlier statement (moving the case of the dispute)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מחלוקת was about a field and a tree.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מחלוקת is only about a בור and a שובך. For a field and a tree, everyone agrees there is מעילה on the item and its contents.

steps.title: What is the argument about when they are empty, and when they are full?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the two תנאים argue about with an empty cistern or dovecote, and with a full one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about a cistern and a dovecote: when they are empty, what do they argue about? And when they are full, what do they argue about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. It wants to understand the argument in two situations: an empty cistern or dovecote, and a full one. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the argument is only about a cistern and a dovecote, the גמרא splits it into two cases. Each case may rest on a different reason. Step 4 answers the empty case, and steps 8-9 answer the full case.

phrases.english: And regarding a cistern and a dovecote:
when they are empty, about what do they disagree,
and when they are full, about what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the reworded statement and asks what each side's reasoning is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the reason for the מחלוקת is in the empty case and in the full case of a בור and a שובך

steps.title: Empty case: the dispute between רבי מאיר and the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: When the cistern or dovecote is empty, the argument is the same as the one between רבי מאיר and the רבנן about transferring a דבר שלא בא לעולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they are empty, they argue about the same thing רבי מאיר and the רבנן argue about. The תנא קמא holds like the רבנן, who say a person cannot transfer something that does not exist yet. רבי אלעזר בר' שמעון holds like רבי מאיר, who says a person can transfer something that does not exist yet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the empty case. It ties it to a well-known argument about whether you can give away something that does not exist yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An empty cistern or dovecote has nothing in it. So consecrating its "contents" means consecrating future water or doves, which is a דבר שלא בא לעולם. The תנא קמא says this does not work, so there is no מעילה on the contents. רבי אלעזר בר' שמעון says it does work.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the teaching
Something that does not exist yet

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of דבר שלא בא לעולם comes up all over ש"ס in sales, gifts and הקדש. Here it explains a case about מעילה.

phrases.english: When they are empty,
they disagree in the dispute
of Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis;
for the first tanna holds like the Rabbis,
who say: A person cannot transfer ownership of
something that has not come into the world;
and Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon,
holds like Rabbi Meir, who says:

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם מַקְנֶה דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: A person can transfer ownership of something that has not come into the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרֵיקָנִין פְּלִיגִי בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the שאלה (the empty case).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The empty case depends on whether one can transfer a דבר שלא בא לעולם: the תנא קמא follows the רבנן, and רבי אלעזר בר' שמעון follows רבי מאיר.

steps.title: רבי מאיר only spoke about things that are likely to come
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that רבי מאיר allowed this only for things that are expected to come, like dates from a palm tree. Who says water or doves will ever come?
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say that you heard רבי מאיר say this about things like the fruit of a palm tree, which are likely to come. But these, water and doves, who says they will come?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison to רבי מאיר. His view may only cover things that are expected to come into existence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A palm tree normally produces fruit, so its future dates are fairly certain. Water in a cistern and doves in a dovecote may never show up. So רבי מאיר might not allow transferring them, and the explanation in step 4 would fall apart.

phrases.english: You can say that you heard Rabbi Meir say this
in a case such as the fruit of a palm tree,
which are likely to come;
these, who says they will come?
phrases.notes: "These" means the water and doves of the empty cistern and dovecote.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison made in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: Linking רבי אלעזר בר' שמעון to רבי מאיר's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר may only allow transferring things that are likely to come into existence, and water or doves may never come.

steps.title: רבא: cases where the water or doves are expected to come
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives cases where the contents are expected to come: rainwater flowing from his courtyard into the cistern, and doves coming from his other dovecote.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can find such a case. For example, water that flows through his courtyard into the cistern, or doves that come from his other dovecote into this dovecote.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא saves the comparison by pointing to cases where the water or doves are expected to arrive, much like the dates of a palm tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If rain runs from the man's courtyard straight into his cistern, water will very likely come. If his full dovecote sends doves into the empty one, doves will very likely come. In these cases the contents are like palm fruit, so רבי מאיר's view does apply.

keyTerms.meaning: You can find such a case

steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת is only about a בור and a שובך. In the empty case, it depends on the debate over transferring a דבר שלא בא לעולם, in cases where the water or doves are expected to come.

phrases.english: Rava said: You can find it
with water that comes by way of his courtyard into the cistern,
and doves that come
by way of his dovecote into the dovecote.
phrases.notes: He means his other dovecote, which is full and sends doves into this empty one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Water and doves are uncertain, so רבי מאיר's view would not apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is one where the water or doves are expected to come, so they are like palm fruit and רבי מאיר's view applies.

steps.title: What is the argument when the cistern or dovecote is full?
steps.stepSummary: After explaining the empty case, the גמרא asks what the two תנאים argue about when the בור or שובך is already full.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when they are full, what do they argue about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finished the empty case and now asks about the full case. This short question sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the empty case, the argument was about הקדש of something that does not exist yet (דבר שלא בא לעולם). When the water or doves are already there, that reason no longer works. So the גמרא needs a different explanation for the full case.

keyTerms.meaning: Full: the cistern already has water, or the dovecote already has doves

phrases.english: And with full ones, about what do they argue?
phrases.notes: "Full ones" means a cistern that already has water, or a dovecote that already has doves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 3 asked about both the empty and the full case. Steps 4-6 handled the empty case. Now the גמרא turns to the second half of that question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the basis of the מחלוקת when the בור or שובך already contains water or doves?

steps.title: רבא: he consecrated the cistern without mentioning the water
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the case is someone who consecrated a בור סתם. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון follows his father's rule that we learn הקדש from an ordinary sale. A seller can sell the cistern without the water, so only the cistern becomes הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The case is where someone consecrated a cistern without saying anything more. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds like his father, who said we learn the law of הקדש from the law of an ordinary person. In a regular sale, the seller can say: 'I sold you the cistern, not the water.' So too with הקדש: 'I consecrated the cistern, not the water.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the full case. The person said only 'the בור', and the question is whether the water inside is included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's rule is that הקדש (דין גבוה) works the same way as a deal between regular people (דין הדיוט). In a sale, 'the cistern' does not automatically include the water. So when someone consecrates 'the cistern', the water stays his, and there is no מעילה on it.

keyTerms.meaning: He consecrated: gave the item to the בית המקדש
Without saying anything more about it
We learn the law of הקדש from the law of an ordinary sale between people
An ordinary person, as opposed to הקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sides. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון is the one who says the water is NOT consecrated, because he compares הקדש to a sale.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהִקְדִּישׁ בּוֹר סְתָם;
phrases.english: Rava said: For example, where he consecrated a cistern without specifying;
phrases.notes: He just said "the cistern" and did not say whether the water was included.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לַהּ כַּאֲבוּהּ,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon holds like his father,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: דָּנִין דִּין גָּבוֹהַּ מִדִּין הֶדְיוֹט,
phrases.english: who said: We learn the law of the Most High from the law of an ordinary person,
phrases.notes: "The Most High" means הקדש, things given to the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: just as with the law of an ordinary person, he can say:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּירָא זַבֵּינִי לָךְ, מַיָּא לָא זַבֵּינִי לָךְ;
phrases.english: I sold you the cistern, I did not sell you the water;
so too the law of the Most High:
he consecrated the cistern, he did not consecrate the water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהִקְדִּישׁ בּוֹר סְתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 by defining the case and giving רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's reasoning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is where he consecrated the בור סתם. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון compares הקדש to a sale, where the water is not included, so the water is not consecrated.

steps.title: The תנא קמא does not compare הקדש to a sale
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא holds that we do not learn הקדש from an ordinary sale, so the water is consecrated together with the cistern.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא קמא holds: We do not learn the law of הקדש from the law of an ordinary person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבא's answer by giving the other side's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the תנא קמא does not apply sale rules to הקדש, he is not limited by 'I sold the cistern, not the water.' That is why, when a full בור is consecrated, he holds there is מעילה on the water inside too. This is the reverse of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The first תנא, the first opinion quoted in the ברייתא
We do not learn one case from the other

steps.whatToRemember: The full-case מחלוקת is about one question: is הקדש judged like an ordinary sale (דנין דין גבוה מדין הדיוט) or not?

phrases.english: And the first Tanna holds:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין דָּנִין דִּין גָּבוֹהַּ מִדִּין הֶדְיוֹט.
phrases.english: We do not learn the law of the Most High from the law of an ordinary person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: אֵין דָּנִין דִּין גָּבוֹהַּ מִדִּין הֶדְיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer by giving the opposing view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא rejects the comparison of הקדש to a sale, so the water is included in the הקדש.

steps.title: But our משנה says selling a cistern includes its water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that in a regular sale the water is not included, because the משנה says that one who sold a cistern sold its water.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in an ordinary sale, is the water really not included? But we learned in a משנה: If he sold a cistern, he sold its water!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the assumption behind רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's reasoning. The point under attack is that a seller can keep the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 depended on the idea that in an ordinary sale the water is not included. Our משנה says the opposite: the water does go with the cistern. If that is the rule for a sale, then comparing הקדש to a sale would include the water too, and the explanation falls apart.

phrases.english: And with the law of an ordinary person, it is not so?!
phrases.notes: He means: is it really true that in a regular sale the water is not included?

phrases.english: But we learned: If he sold a cistern, he sold its water!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the sale rule ('I sold you the cistern, not the water') that step 8 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 8 that in an ordinary sale the water is not sold with the cistern.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה rules that selling a cistern includes its water, which goes against the sale rule step 8 assumed.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה follows the lone view of רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the משנה follows only one opinion, רבי נתן. A ברייתא shows that the other view holds the water is not sold with the cistern.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Our משנה is a single opinion. As a ברייתא teaches: If he sold a cistern, he did not sell its water. רבי נתן says: If he sold a cistern, he sold its water.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends step 8 by showing that the משנה's ruling is only one side of a מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא records a מחלוקת about sales. The first view says the water is not included, and רבי נתן says it is. Our משנה follows רבי נתן, so רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון can rely on the other view, where the water stays with the seller.

keyTerms.meaning: A single person's opinion, not everyone's view

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that selling a cistern includes its water is רבי נתן's view. Others hold the water is not included, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's comparison to a sale is built on that view.

phrases.english: Rava said: Our Mishnah is a lone opinion,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: מָכַר בּוֹר – לֹא מָכַר מֵימָיו.
phrases.english: as it is taught: If he sold a cistern, he did not sell its water.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: מָכַר בּוֹר – מָכַר מֵימָיו.
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says: If he sold a cistern, he sold its water.
phrases.notes: This is the opinion our משנה follows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 by limiting the משנה to רבי נתן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a single opinion (משנה יחידאה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be the accepted rule for everyone, that a sale of a cistern includes its water.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי נתן alone. The first view in the ברייתא says the water is not sold, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון can rely on that view.
